cards.b: A learned ability to bring about a result with maximum certainty and minimum effort or time.
Skills are learned; abilities are inherited and underlie skills.
Affected by the environment; the performer must adapt, e.g. a pass in football.
Environment stable and predictable; same each time, e.g. a golf putt.
Gross: large muscle groups (shot put). Fine: small precise movements (darts).
Self-paced: performer controls timing (serve). Externally paced: timing set by others (returning a serve).
Massed: no rest. Distributed: rests or changes between. Distributed suits complex or dangerous skills.
Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Recorded (or Realistic), Time-bound.
Demonstrations, videos, diagrams. Good for beginners.
Coach physically moves the performer. Good for safety and confidence.
Equipment support such as floats or a harness.
From the performer’s own senses, e.g. how the shot felt.
KR: outcome (score, time). KP: how the movement was done (technique).
Intrinsic: from within (enjoyment). Extrinsic: from rewards (trophies, praise).
Performance improves as arousal rises to an optimum, then falls if arousal gets too high.

gaps.s: A skill that must be adapted to a changing environment is an ___ skill.
The T in SMART stands for ___.
Spoken instructions from a coach are ___ guidance.
Information about how a skill was performed is knowledge of ___.
Picturing a perfect performance in your head is mental ___.
A snooker shot is an example of a ___ skill.
The level of alertness and readiness to perform is called ___.

short.q: Classify a tennis serve on the self-paced–externally paced continuum and explain.
short.model: It is self-paced because the server decides when to start and how to hit the ball.

short.q: Why do coaches use SMART targets?
short.model: They give a clear, measurable aim with a deadline. This increases motivation and lets the performer track progress.

short.q: Suggest suitable guidance for a beginner learning a new gymnastics skill and justify it.
short.model: Manual guidance with a demonstration. A spotter keeps the gymnast safe and the demonstration shows the shape of the skill.

short.q: Give one advantage of positive feedback and one of negative feedback.
short.model: Positive feedback builds confidence and motivation. Negative feedback shows errors so they can be corrected.

short.q: Describe two ways a performer can control arousal before a penalty.
short.model: Deep breathing and positive self-talk to stay calm, plus imagery of the kick going in.
